title: Fed emergency rate cut before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) holds an emergency meeting after which the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lowered between November 11, 2025 and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

An emergency meeting is defined as any unscheduled meeting called by the Federal Reserve Board or the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) apart from the regular eight pre-scheduled meetings for 2025 and the regular eight pre-scheduled meetings for 2026.

The resolution source will be official announcements from the Federal Reserve’s website (federalreserve.gov) or credible news sources reporting on the emergency meeting.

eventMetadata.context_description: The 92.5% market-implied odds against an emergency Federal Reserve rate cut before 2027 reflect trader consensus on resilient U.S. economic conditions, with inflation data trending toward the 2% target and a labor market showing steady, if moderating, employment growth. Recent FOMC communications have emphasized a data-dependent approach within the existing policy framework, supported by stable Treasury yields and contained volatility measures, which reduce the probability of an inter-meeting action. This pricing aligns with historical precedent where unscheduled cuts occur mainly amid acute financial stress or sharp downturn signals. Realistic scenarios that could shift odds include a sudden banking-sector shock, sharp equity-market decline exceeding 20%, or rapid deterioration in nonfarm payrolls and consumer spending that forces an expedited response ahead of scheduled meetings.
